title: Godot vs GameMaker: Which Fits Your Team in 2026?
description: Godot is free under the MIT license; GameMaker is free for non-commercial use with a $99.99 commercial license. Compare 2D workflow, export and console terms.
intro: GameMaker is a 2D game engine that is free for non-commercial use and needs a $99.99 Professional license to release commercially, while Godot is an MIT-licensed 2D and 3D engine with no paid tier. Both are common first choices for 2D projects. They differ in how you pay for a shipped game, how consoles are handled and how much of the engine you can read. This comparison uses each vendor's own pages to lay out the terms for a small team.
verdict: Pick GameMaker when your project is strictly 2D, you like its GML language and you are happy to pay a one-time fee at release. Pick Godot when you want no license step at all, a dedicated 3D option for later and source access. Console targets change the maths for both, so check that row first.
pick_a: Pick Godot if you want zero licensing steps, might add 3D later, or want to modify the engine itself.
pick_b: Pick GameMaker if the game is 2D only and you prefer a single purpose tool with its own language, a marketplace and a one-time commercial license.

text: GameMaker's get page says the engine is free to download and keep forever for non-commercial use. To make money from a game you buy a Commercial License for $99.99, which is the Professional one-time purchase. That is a small fixed cost, and the page says there is no forced watermark or splash screen on the free tier or either paid tier.

Godot has nothing to buy. Its FAQ places it under the OSI-approved MIT license, and the homepage makes no other pricing statement. The practical effect is that a commercial release needs no license step, only the usual care about the third-party assets you add.
GameMaker reserves console export for the Enterprise subscription, and the pages opened here show no price for it, so ask the vendor before budgeting. Enterprise also adds source code access.

Godot's homepage says consoles are supported through third-party publishers. Neither route is a one-click export, so a console release means a separate cost and a separate partner, whichever engine you start with.

GameMaker is built around 2D and its own language, GML, with tutorials, a marketplace and asset bundles listed on the homepage. A solo developer often values that narrow focus because the tool does one thing.

Godot organizes work in nodes and scenes, offers GDScript and C#, and treats 2D as a dedicated engine rather than a layer on 3D. Its editor and engine are one project, so a feature you miss can in principle be added by you or by the community.
GameMaker is a 2D tool, so a later move to 3D means changing engines. Godot covers both, which lowers that risk, though the homepage describes its 3D as simple rather than as a large-scale renderer.

GameMaker's homepage cites UNDERTALE, Hyper Light Drifter and Chicory: A Colorful Tale as backed titles; Godot's homepage names sponsors such as Scorewarrior, W4 Games, JetBrains and Mega Crit. Both lists show real shipped or funded work, which is useful reassurance but not a substitute for a prototype in each.

faqs.q: Can I sell a game made with the free GameMaker tier?
faqs.a: No. The vendor says the free tier is for non-commercial use, and that making money from a game requires the Commercial License at $99.99, which is the Professional purchase. Console export needs the Enterprise subscription.

faqs.q: Does Godot charge royalties or fees?
faqs.a: Godot's FAQ says it is free and open source under the OSI-approved MIT license, and the homepage states no fees. Check the license file in the repository for your own attribution duties.

faqs.q: Which is easier for someone who has never programmed?
faqs.a: GameMaker uses GML and Godot uses GDScript, both text languages. The opened pages do not compare difficulty, so try each tutorial. GameMaker lists tutorials on its site; Godot's docs include a first 2D game walkthrough.

faqs.q: Will GameMaker put a logo on my game?
faqs.a: The vendor says GameMaker does not force a watermark or splash screen on the free tier or either paid tier, though it would be grateful if you add its logo voluntarily.

faqs.q: Can I move a GameMaker project into Godot?
faqs.a: The pages opened for this comparison say nothing about project conversion, so assume art and audio assets move across while code and scenes are rebuilt. Test with a small slice before committing a full project.

sources.fact: GameMaker is free for non-commercial use; commercial license $99.99; console export needs Enterprise; no forced watermark.
GameMaker homepage lists GML, marketplace, asset bundles, GX.games upload and export targets.
Godot is Free and open source Software available under the OSI-approved MIT license.
Godot's homepage lists node and scene system, GDScript, C#, C++ and GDExtension, dedicated 2D engine and third-party console support.
